options: The result depends on the unpredictable order of operations on shared state
Two processes run the same sequential code on private data
questions.explanation: If the outcome changes when the scheduler changes the interleaving, the program has a race. Private data does not create one.

questions.prompt: Which are requirements of a correct critical-section solution?
options: The critical section must contain a system call
questions.explanation: Mutual exclusion keeps two processes out at once. Progress says outsiders cannot freeze the decision. Bounded waiting caps how long one process can be overtaken.

options: Let only one holder be inside a critical section
questions.explanation: Lock before the shared update, unlock after. A second locker waits. That is mutual exclusion, not a memory-management scheme.

questions.prompt: A counting semaphore initialized to 3 is a natural fit for
options: A single bit in the ALU
questions.explanation: Each acquire decrements the count. At zero the next acquire waits until a release. The initial value is the size of the pool.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT one of the four necessary conditions for deadlock?
questions.explanation: The four conditions are mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, and circular wait. A scheduler name is not one of them.
traps: Replacing “no preemption” with “preemption is allowed”, which is the opposite condition.

options: The starved job could run if the scheduler chose it; a deadlocked set can never proceed
They are two names for the same event
questions.explanation: A starved job is legal to run and keeps losing. Deadlock is a set of jobs whose needed resources are held inside the set.

questions.prompt: In the banker’s algorithm, a state is safe when
options: There exists an order of granting that lets every process finish
Every process already holds its maximum claim
The available vector is zero and nobody can run
questions.explanation: Safety means there is at least one sequence that avoids deadlock from here. It does not mean a deadlock has already happened.

questions.prompt: Forcing a process to request every resource it will need before it starts mainly breaks
options: Mutual exclusion, by sharing a printer mid-line
questions.explanation: If a process holds nothing while it waits for the whole set, it cannot hold one resource and wait for another.

questions.prompt: Name one deadlock condition and a concrete way to break it.
questions.answer: Circular wait can be broken by acquiring resources in one fixed global order, so a cycle cannot close.
questions.explanation: Other valid answers: break hold-and-wait by allocating the whole set at once, or allow preemption of the resource. Mutual exclusion often cannot be broken for a real device.
